subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the trust boundary for outbound-staged generated HTML after resolving the current merge conflict?
rationale: The code shape looks sound, but it deliberately changes which local HTML host-read paths can be trusted, and that security lifecycle is an owner policy decision rather than an automated review choice.

options.title: Accept Provenance Lifecycle
options.body: After a clean rebase, accept the content-bound SQLite marker as the supported trust boundary for staged generated HTML.

options.title: Require Tighter Boundary
options.body: Ask for a narrower lifecycle, different marker owner, bounded TTL behavior, or additional upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Keep Staging Fail-Closed
options.body: Pause or close this PR and keep generated HTML blocked after outbound staging until a different security model is chosen.

recommendation.title: Accept Provenance Lifecycle
recommendation.body: After a clean rebase, accept the content-bound SQLite marker as the supported trust boundary for staged generated HTML.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored and merged the original trusted generated HTML host-read behavior that this PR extends.
